0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 28 November 1986, after the draft finalized by the Cement and Concrete Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 0.2 In recent years, there has been a growing awareness that exposure to asbestos dust can have harmful effects on the health of workers. In order to give guidance on how the risk of exposure to asbestos dust can be prevented, controlled or minimized, it was felt necessary to lay down some standards regarding safe use of different products containing asbestos, improving conditions in workplaces, preventive measures, protection and supervision of the health of workers, packaging, transport This standard lays down the and disposal of asbestos waste, etc. recommendations for disposal of asbestos waste material. 0.3 In the formulation of this standard, due weightage has been given to international co-ordination among the standards and practices prevailing in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices in the field in this country. This has been met by deriving assistance from `II,0 Codes of Practice: Safety in the use of asbestos', 1984 published by International Labour Office, Geneva and Schedule XIV on `Handling and processing of asbestos', framed under Section 87 of Factories Act.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard lays down the asbestos waste materials without asbestos dust. 2. OBJECT 2.1 The objects of this standard are as follows: recommendations for significant generation disposal of of airborne

a) To prevent the risk of exposure to airborne asbestos fibre dust during collection, transportation and disposal of wastes arising out of mining and milling of asbestos, manufacturing and usage of asbestos products. 3

b) To eliminate the probability of release of airborne asbestos intd general environment out of the wastes disposed of, 3. APPLICATION 3.1 The provisions form of asbestos disposed of. 4. REQUIREMENTS

5.1 Every employer who undertakes work which is liable to generate asbestos containing waste, shall take adequate steps to prevent and/or reduce the generation of airborne asbestos dust during handling, storing, transportation and final disposal of asbestos and asbestos containing products. - The most desirable method of controlling 5.2 Waste Avoidance waste is to minimize the amount of waste that is generated. This is generally done by recycling the waste and choosing a process or operation that reduces generation of waste.

DISPOSAL OF WASTE 9.1 General 9.1.1 Before a site is used for the disposal of asbestos waste, care shall be taken to establish-&hat the site is suitable, and accepta@e for, the purpose. 9.1.2 The disposal site chosen shall have vehicular access to the ing face or to a hole or trench dug to receive the asbestos waste. work-

9.1.3 The waste shall, wherever practicable, be deposited at the foot of the working face of the landfill site or at the bottom of an excavation dug for it. 9.1.4 Where the waste has to be deposited from above the working face, or into fin excavation, care shall be taken to prevent spillage, 9.13 When deposited, all waste other than high'density wasteshall be covered to an acceptable depth, say 200 to 250 mm, as soon a$ possible. No asbestos waste other than high density waste shall be left uncovered at the end of a working day. 9.1.6 Final covering shall be to a minimum of asbesros waste, other than high 1 depth of 2 m. density waste,

9.1.7 If wet waste is deposited, it shall be covered in the same way as ,. dry waste to prevent the escape of asbestos aust on drying out. 9.1.8 Wet pits should not normally asbestos waste other than high density be used material. for the disposal of any

9.1.9 Where high density waste is'deposited on a dry site, care shall be taken to ensure that it is not ground to dust by the passage of vehicles over it. 9.1.10 The disposal sites for asbestos and public entry shall be restricted. waste shall be clearly demarcated
